method.scoring: All three dimensions assessed separately against complete accepted facts and complete STOP final text; no added educational content and no averaging. Aesthetic/method/timebox preferences do not cause failure.
method.blindingLimitation: Neutral A01–A08 IDs conceal execution mapping and per-case provider/config labels until lock. The reviewer previously signed the original tasks and gold mixture, and knows from the task authorization that the run used DeepSeek only. This is not full blinding.

assessments.rationale: The actual totals and known overclaim are addressed without reteaching secure value reading or requiring a climate archive. A bounded near-transfer check, explicit unsupported claim and independent stopping gate are useful. The claim about comparisons across stations is broader than needed for a local station trend but does not require unavailable work.
assessments.representativeOutputQuote: Then make limits of trend inference the main effort: have the learner write one claim that the three one-year, one-station values do support

issues.requirementQuote: Prepare to read monthly rainfall totals and explain what the data can and cannot establish about a longer-term trend.
issues.outputQuote: a climate trend requires multi-year data, appropriate comparison across years and stations
issues.consequence: The wording can imply multiple stations are always needed for a local station trend; that geographic generalization is unnecessary here. It does not compel an archive or alter the correct conclusion about the three supplied months.
issues.resolution: Qualify comparisons as appropriate to the claim's geographic scope; multi-year observations of the same station can address a local long-term question.

assessments.stoppingGate: Stop when learner independently interprets data, rejects unsupported trend, states missing evidence and passes one transfer item.
assessments.resources: Supplied 40/70/50 mm data, labels and explicitly created practice; no archive/forecasting.
assessments.admissibleAlternatives: Any valid comparisons and justified data-limited claims remain possible; no compulsory multi-station archive.
assessments.verbatimFinalText: {"strategy":"Work backward from the accepted outcome: justified interpretation of monthly rainfall data, and the fixed deadline. Because the learner already reads values correctly, do not spend primary effort on basic value reading. First, briefly verify graph units and comparisons: confirm the unit is millimetres and make the supplied comparisons from January 40 mm, February 70 mm and March 50 mm (February highest; March between January and February). Then make limits of trend inference the main effort: have the learner write one claim that the three one-year, one-station values do support ('this year at this station, February was the wettest of these three months') and one they do not support ('the climate is getting wetter'). Require an explicit reason: a climate trend requires multi-year data, appropriate comparison across years and stations, and separation of short-term variation from longer-term change. Correctness checks: units and labels; correct month order and differences; claim wording limited to the data; identification of the missing evidence; no archive fetching or meteorological forecasting. Use supplied or explicitly created practice values for one near-transfer item with a different pattern and ask for one justified and one overclaim. Dependencies: accurate reading and comparison precede the limits-of-inference work; do not move on if comparisons are wrong. Effort: no official weighting is supplied, so priority rests on the observed overclaim and its direct link to the outcome; use about the preferred 15 minutes, not a broad climate project. Uncertainty: exam importance and mark weight are unknown; do not claim typical frequency or marks. Stop when the learner independently gives a defensible interpretation, correctly labels the overclaim as unsupported, states the missing evidence, and passes one transfer item. Defer historical archive retrieval, forecasting, and broad climate science."}

assessments.rationale: The strategy targets the consent-aware outline, includes an open question, concrete-event follow-up and correction invitation, checks all four supplied brief requirements, and preserves recording/editing/account checking as later unbooked scope. The learner drafts/self-checks rather than merely attends.
assessments.representativeOutputQuote: Meaningful stopping point: a checked question outline that can elicit one concrete remembered event and includes consent and correction.
assessments.stoppingGate: Stop at a checked outline with consent/correction that can elicit a remembered event; revise once if initial check fails and do not claim a failing outline passed.
assessments.resources: Supplied project brief and willing interviewee; no interview date, recording or software needed now.
assessments.admissibleAlternatives: Different non-leading questions, outline formats or self-check/optional verbal test can satisfy the gate. One page is a modest format suggestion, not an additional educational milestone.
assessments.verbatimFinalText: {"strategy":"Treat this as a beginner, consent-first question-design checkpoint, not the whole oral history project. Use a short, comfortable work period, ideally around the preferred 15 minutes: briefly model oral-history ethics and question types, then have the learner draft and self-check a one-page outline aimed at eliciting one specific remembered event. Prioritize permission language, one non-leading open lead question, at least one follow-up asking for a concrete time, place, action, or sensory detail, and an explicit invitation for the speaker to correct or clarify the account. Correctness checks should verify the outline against the brief's four requirements, screen for leading or compound questions, and confirm wording stays speaker-centered. If the outline fails, revise once; if it passes, stop. Dependencies: a willing interviewee is identified but no date or recording exists, so no recording, editing, or software is needed now. Recording, selecting/editing audio, and full account-checking remain later strategic scope, unbooked unless fresh evidence and an explicit request justify them. Uncertainty: the learner has never designed an interview and the chosen event may need calibration, so keep the outline simple and optionally test it verbally. Meaningful stopping point: a checked question outline that can elicit one concrete remembered event and includes consent and correction. Do not schedule the interview or begin recording or editing at this checkpoint."}

assessments.rationale: It uses supplied and unfamiliar passages, requires three-way classification and textual justification, prioritizes the actually reported plausibility error, and does not invent exam weights. The claim that inference has already been demonstrated/partly performed is not grounded as learner evidence; however, the independent gate still checks inference alongside both other categories, so this attribution does not remove required work or certify false readiness.
assessments.representativeOutputQuote: Stop when the learner independently classifies and justifies all three categories across two unseen passages with no overreach into background assumptions

issues.requirementQuote: The learner can find a direct quotation but treats plausible background stories as established facts.
issues.outputQuote: Evidence shows literal quotation is already partly secure, inferential reading is demonstrated in the sample passage
issues.additionalOutputQuote: Inference practice focuses on the evidence-to-conclusion link already partly performed.
issues.consequence: The supplied correct passage classification is an instructional example, not a demonstrated learner inference performance. This overstates readiness, but final independent checks still cover inference and priority remains the real unsupported-claim weakness.
issues.resolution: Describe supplied inference as a model/example and treat learner inference readiness as unverified pending the first check.

assessments.stoppingGate: Independently classify/justify all three categories across two unseen passages without background overreach.
assessments.resources: Supplied library passage plus unfamiliar short passages can be explicitly created; no external answer resource required.
assessments.admissibleAlternatives: Quoted or paraphrased evidence and an explanation of what is missing are valid; the exercise count and preferred timeboxes are a bounded approach rather than a universal floor.
assessments.verbatimFinalText: {"strategy":"Work backwards from the fixed 2026-10-14 assessment and the accepted task (passage-based distinction and explanation checks, no grammar drills, no mark predictions). Because assessment weights are unknown, do not rank topics by assumed marks; rank by actual readiness and dependency. Evidence shows literal quotation is already partly secure, inferential reading is demonstrated in the sample passage, but unsupported claims are conflated with background assumptions — that is the priority. Plan roughly two 15-minute timeboxes on 12–13 Oct (comfortable-early, moderate), leaving exam day for a short confidence warm-up only if the learner wants it; this stays well under available capacity, since nothing justifies saturation. Session shape: use the supplied library passage first, then one or two unfamiliar short passages. For each candidate statement, the learner must (a) label it stated, defensible inference, or unsupported, and (b) justify with a quoted or paraphrased line, or state what the passage would need to say to support it. Literal reading gets only one quick verification check rather than re-teaching. Inference practice focuses on the evidence-to-conclusion link already partly performed. Unsupported claims get the most repetitions, especially plausible-sounding additions such as invented waiting, motives, or timelines. Correctness check: require text-anchored justification every time, and correct any label justified only by plausibility. Stop when the learner independently classifies and justifies all three categories across two unseen passages with no overreach into background assumptions — then stop rather than adding volume. Uncertainty to state plainly: skill importance and relative weighting are unverified, so time is allocated by dependency and observed weakness, not by predicted exam return."}

assessments.rationale: Correctly distinguishes valid modus-ponens form from converse, gives P=false,Q=true counterexample, seeks unfamiliar valid/invalid decisions and bounded explanations, allows either table or counterexample, and makes remediation conditional. It falsely states that no formal assessment exists, rather than saying none is supplied; no consequential choice depends on that absence claim.
assessments.representativeOutputQuote: Accept any correct bounded justification; do not require symbols or formal proof machinery.

issues.requirementQuote: The learner knows these words but has not evaluated an unfamiliar argument.
issues.outputQuote: no prior learning evidence and no formal assessment exist
issues.consequence: No formal assessment is supplied, but that does not prove none exists. The bounded method/check does not depend on that categorical absence.
issues.resolution: Say no formal-assessment details are supplied rather than asserting none exists.

assessments.stoppingGate: Independent correct decision plus bounded justification on a new mixed item; retention check is conditional on later revisiting, not a scheduled quota.
assessments.resources: Supplied truth conditions and self-created concrete arguments; no proof notation, external tutor/key or formal assessment needed.
assessments.admissibleAlternatives: Any bounded valid justification, four-row table or explicit counterexample is admitted.
assessments.verbatimFinalText: {"strategy":"Treat this as a short mastery-oriented reasoning task. Begin with a brief diagnostic using a concrete if-then statement to surface the learner’s current rule, then restate the operative truth condition: P implies Q is false only when P is true and Q is false. Prioritize two linked capabilities: applying truth conditions to test when a conditional is false, and distinguishing valid inference (from P implies Q and P, conclude Q) from the invalid converse (from P implies Q and Q, infer P). Learner actions: for each unfamiliar simple argument, identify P and Q, state the premises, then try to make the premises true and the conclusion false; for the converse, give the explicit counterexample P=false, Q=true; for the valid form, explain why no counterexample exists under the truth conditions. Accept any correct bounded justification; do not require symbols or formal proof machinery. Correctness checks: the learner independently decides at least one fresh valid item and one fresh invalid or converse item, compares justifications to the truth conditions, and resolves any contradiction. Proportionate effort: fit within the preferred 15-minute window at moderate intensity, comfortable early; stop when the learner can independently transfer the method to a new mixed item and explain the decision, with no fixed practice quota or stage ceremony. Dependencies: truth conditions before converse analysis, with a four-row table or P=false, Q=true example as concrete remediation if the converse error persists. Uncertainty: no prior learning evidence and no formal assessment exist, so treat explanations as evidence and do not let timers or self-report certify mastery. A meaningful stopping point is an independent correct decision plus bounded justification on a new item, with a brief retention check when the topic is revisited."}

assessments.rationale: The first-card strategy is otherwise bounded and locally feasible, preserves supplied description and future scope, and acknowledges no image exists. Its explicit present/nonempty alt-attribute correctness gate nevertheless applies to the selected placeholder route. The accepted facts allow a text placeholder plus explanation of future-image alternative text; a normal text placeholder has no image alt attribute. The gate rejects that allowed artifact and can teach meaningless alt markup on text containers. This needs substantive criterion/instruction correction.
assessments.representativeOutputQuote: Correctness checks: file opens without error in a browser; exactly one heading for the card; description matches source wording; alt attribute is present and descriptive, not empty or decorative;

issues.requirementQuote: No object image file is supplied. The first card may use a text placeholder and explain the alternative text that an actual image would need.
issues.outputQuote: an image element — or an explicit placeholder — carrying a meaningful alt attribute
issues.additionalOutputQuote: alt attribute is present and descriptive, not empty or decorative
issues.consequence: The accepted text-placeholder branch can meet the goal with visible text and explanation, yet it fails the mandatory attribute gate. A beginner can be taught that alt on an arbitrary text placeholder provides image accessibility semantics. The first-card completion check is therefore incorrect for an expressly allowed route.
issues.resolution: Apply present/descriptive alt only when a real img element is used. For a text placeholder, check the readable placeholder and a separate explanation/sentence of the alternative text a future image would need. Do not require a missing image asset.
issues.severityRationale: This is a substantive instruction/criterion defect against a consequential accepted alternative, rather than a preference for one tag, format or timebox. It requires adjudication; a permissible image-placeholder implementation does not repair the output's unconditional gate for text placeholders.

assessments.stoppingGate: The strategy ends at independent rebuilding plus alt explanation, but its mandatory alt-attribute gate incorrectly governs a permitted text-placeholder card. The coherent smaller artifact is a resume checkpoint, not a claim of completion.
assessments.resources: Text editor/browser and supplied description are available/feasible; no image asset required. Future image-alt sentence is feasible; alt attribute applies to an actual image element, not arbitrary text.
assessments.admissibleAlternatives: Plain text placeholder with a separate meaningful future-image alternative-text explanation must remain admissible. Semantic article/section or heading choices are not the reason for failure.
assessments.verbatimFinalText: {"strategy":"Treat the accepted request as a single learn-by-doing prerequisite checkpoint, not the exhibit itself: producing one locally opened HTML file that renders an accessible object card for the blue ceramic bowl. Approach: brief worked demonstration of the minimum semantic skeleton, then guided practice where the learner types and adjusts it themselves and reopens the file in a browser to see the effect. Priorities in order: (1) a valid HTML document container that opens locally by double-click; (2) one card region (article or section) with a single correct heading; (3) the supplied description reproduced faithfully as body text (\"Blue bowl with a chipped rim.\"); (4) an image element — or an explicit placeholder — carrying a meaningful alt attribute, with a short explanation of why alt text must describe the object rather than repeat the caption or filename. Because no image file is supplied, teach the placeholder route and have the learner write the exact alt sentence a real photo would need (e.g. a blue ceramic bowl with a chipped rim). Defer navigation, visual/CSS polish, and publication: these are included strategic scope but unbooked and require no activity now, so record them as later milestones only. Correctness checks: file opens without error in a browser; exactly one heading for the card; description matches source wording; alt attribute is present and descriptive, not empty or decorative; learner can state, unaided, what would break for a screen-reader user if alt were missing. Effort is small and should finish promptly — one comfortable session of about 15 minutes within the ample daily capacity — with the stopping point being the learner independently rebuilding the card without copying and explaining the alt-text choice. If time runs short, stop at a coherent smaller artifact (document plus heading and description) and resume there. Dependencies: a plain text editor and any browser; no framework, JavaScript, hosting, account or image asset. Uncertainty is low about scope and mechanics but higher about transfer to the next object, so later expansion (second/third card, navigation, styling, publication) should wait for fresh evidence and an explicit request."}

assessments.rationale: Independent changed production/explanation, es/está accents, conditional bounded help and honest unknown retention all match the task. A few fresh sentences and mixed contexts can be proportionate here. The optional different-pronouns example should be kept to third-person singular compatible with supplied forms; other persons would create an unsupported conjugation dependency, but the output also offers valid different-name/same-form contexts.
assessments.representativeOutputQuote: Apply bounded remediation only if the distinction actually fails: restate the supplied rule, show one minimal contrast pair built from the learner's own chosen name, then ask for one new sentence plus re-explanation.

issues.requirementQuote: Names and occupations may be learner-chosen; use supplied forms es/está. No external tutor or exercise key is available.
issues.outputQuote: a couple of fresh contexts such as different people, pronouns, or a person who is both a teacher and currently tired
issues.consequence: Unqualified pronoun variation could invite forms outside es/está. The examples are alternatives and third-person-singular variation is valid, so this does not compel unavailable conjugation learning.
issues.resolution: Keep names/pronouns compatible with es/está and do not introduce a new conjugation dependency.

assessments.stoppingGate: Novel correct sentences covering both uses, accurate explanations and one transfer item; if one remediation cycle still fails, record not mastered and stop. Retention suggestion is optional/unfixed.
assessments.resources: Supplied teacher rule/models and learner-chosen names/occupations; self-check acknowledged unverified, no tutor/key claimed.
assessments.admissibleAlternatives: Different names or third-person-singular pronouns with es/está; no requirement to use first/second person, other tenses or every ser/estar use.
assessments.verbatimFinalText: {"strategy":"Target demonstrated mastery of only the two bounded items — occupation with \"es\" and current tiredness with \"está\" — within the learner's stated comfortable-early, moderate, ~15-minute preference, not coverage of other ser/estar uses. Spend the first minutes on a quick recall of the two supplied models, then move almost all time to the core evidence: the learner independently produces changed sentences, using self-chosen names, occupations and tiredness statements, and must not reuse \"Ana es profesora\" or \"Ana está cansada.\" Treat three things as separate evidence rather than one: (1) changed production with the correct verb and preserved \"está\"; (2) an accurate rule explanation (occupation → ser; current state/tiredness → estar); (3) transfer, i.e., a couple of fresh contexts such as different people, pronouns, or a person who is both a teacher and currently tired. A correct verb with a wrong explanation, a right explanation over a recycled sentence, or a correct sentence on the known models only does not count as mastery. Apply bounded remediation only if the distinction actually fails: restate the supplied rule, show one minimal contrast pair built from the learner's own chosen name, then ask for one new sentence plus re-explanation. Cap this at a single cycle; if it still fails, stop and record the distinction as not yet mastered instead of drilling. Because no external tutor or exercise key exists, every check is self-checked against the stated rule and the accented \"está\"; record self-report as evidence but acknowledge it is unverified and cannot certify readiness. Keep effort proportionate: one or two short sittings across the available window only if needed, no stage ceremony and no practice quota. Meaningful stopping point: the learner has produced several independent, novel correct sentences covering both scope items, explained each choice accurately, and passed one transfer item — then stop, optionally noting that a brief retention re-check on a later day would be informative, without fixing a date. Priorities if time is short: changed production first, explanation second, transfer third. Known uncertainties: the learner currently only recognizes the models; retention and durability beyond the session are unknown."}

assessments.rationale: It computes all actual bars correctly, repairs the two-eighths misconception, offers all expressly allowed counting modalities and stops after actual worksheet explanation/check. No invented worksheet, recording/attendance or broad mastery claim.
assessments.stoppingGate: Learner explains each assigned bar and each sums to four; only error-triggered corrective recount.
assessments.resources: Supplied q/e key and all three assigned bars; no external resources.
assessments.admissibleAlternatives: Written, spoken or clapped counting remain equally valid; equivalent sum notation is accepted.
assessments.verbatimFinalText: {"strategy":"Use brief direct instruction plus guided practice: confirm the supplied note values (q = one beat; e = half a beat) and that a 4/4 bar totals four, then have the learner count aloud, write, or clap each assigned bar and explain each note's contribution. Priority is correcting the known misconception that two eighth notes are two whole beats; prompt the learner to group each e-e pair as one beat. Check correctness by summing each bar: A = q q q q = 4; B = q e e q q = 1 + 1/2 + 1/2 + 1 + 1 = 4; C = e e e e q q = 1/2+1/2+1/2+1/2+1+1 = 4, and by asking the learner to re-explain any bar that does not total four. Proportionate effort: use about 10–15 minutes, comfortable early, with no recording or teacher attendance required; do not invent extra exercises or claim broader mastery. If the learner still treats eighths as whole beats, give one concrete correction and re-count that bar; otherwise stop. Dependencies are the supplied note values and the three assigned bars only. Stopping point: after the learner explains the three bars using the supplied note values and each bar checks as four beats; add no more unless an error triggers the single corrective re-count."}

assessments.rationale: Directly performs the four actual annotation moves, distinguishes observation from opinion, quotes source text and gives a specific limit without invented sources/attendees/extra annotations. It overstates that uncertainty is necessarily resolved by one checking pass; the actual stopping gate still requires a correct annotation and the revision path does not automatically certify failure as success.
assessments.representativeOutputQuote: Stop when the annotation contains all four requirements, the quote matches the source, and the interpretation is worded as the author's view, not a count of everyone's opinion.

issues.requirementQuote: Complete and check the actual annotation; stop when all four assigned requirements are satisfied.
issues.outputQuote: both are resolved by the checking pass itself
issues.consequence: A checking pass can reveal a persisting misconception rather than resolve it automatically. The separate final gate requires actual correct annotation, so the statement does not certify an incorrect product.
issues.resolution: Say the pass tests these uncertainties; record/revise an unresolved distinction instead of promising resolution.

assessments.stoppingGate: All four requirements present, quote matches source and interpretation remains the author's view rather than everyone's opinions.
assessments.resources: Complete supplied diary entry and assignment; no other source needed/claimed.
assessments.admissibleAlternatives: Any grounded evidential limit remains admissible; two-line distinction and draft/check order are useful methods, not exclusive requirements.
assessments.verbatimFinalText: {"strategy":"Treat this as bounded homework completion, not a study project: work directly on the four assigned moves and stop as soon as all four are present and checked. Sequence them in the order given — (1) name the observed event (six people leaving before the vote), (2) name the interpretation ('I think everyone disliked the proposal'), (3) quote the supporting words verbatim from the diary, (4) state one evidential limit — because each move depends on the one before it. The critical correctness risk is the learner's habit of reading the author's inference as a headcount of all attendees' opinions; pre-empt this by having the learner keep two labelled lines, 'what the author saw' versus 'what the author concluded', and check that the second line still says 'thinks' or 'believes' rather than stating a fact about every attendee. Verify quotes character-for-character against the supplied sentence, and verify the limit is genuinely about this source (single participant's diary, no other source supplied, so it cannot establish what all attendees felt) rather than a generic disclaimer. If the learner collapses the distinction, do not add new sources or invented attendees; re-ask only which words are observation and which are inference, then let them revise. Effort is proportionate to a 15-minute comfortable-early block at moderate intensity: one pass to draft all four elements, one pass to check quotes and the observation/interpretation split. Uncertainty is limited to whether the learner can hold the distinction unaided and whether a stated limit is specific enough; both are resolved by the checking pass itself. Stop when the annotation contains all four requirements, the quote matches the source, and the interpretation is worded as the author's view, not a count of everyone's opinion."}
